name: Bacteriophage Defense Systems (R-M and CRISPR)
description: E. coli defends against bacteriophage infection through multiple systems: (1) Restriction-Modification (R-M) systems where restriction endonucleases (e.g., EcoRI, EcoRV) cleave unmethylated foreign DNA while methyltransferases protect self DNA, (2) CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity where Cas proteins integrate phage DNA sequences into CRISPR array, transcribe crRNAs, and use them to guide Cas nucleases to destroy matching phage DNA. Additional defenses include abortive infection systems and prophage-encoded immunity. Multiple OR gates for alternative defense mechanisms and phage types.
scientificAccuracy: Based on comprehensive research on bacterial defense systems. Nobel Prize to Doudna and Charpentier for CRISPR.
